# PR #215 review — feat(github): inspect installation token metadata (eb0acba vs e4d6657)

Verdict: no confirmed defects found. All high-risk trigger areas check out; tests pass (github pkg 20/20, emulate api 11/11, adapter-next 17/17, adapter-nuxt 17/17 run locally at the frozen head). Findings below are hardening observations and residual risks only.

## Verified invariants (with evidence)

1. Inspection endpoint exposes no secret material.
packages/@emulators/github/src/routes/installation-tokens.ts:7-35 projects only: app id/slug/name, installation id, account id/login/type, permissions, repository_selection/ids, issued_at/expires_at, status. No token string, no private key, no webhook secret, and no token-derived identifier. Collection.insert only adds id/created_at/updated_at (packages/@emulators/core/src/store.ts:106-111), none secret. Tests assert the minted ghs_ token and its 12-char prefix never appear in the payload (webhook-installation.test.ts:527-529), and the token still works while metadata says "expired" (webhook-installation.test.ts:537-544).

2. Reset clears minted authorization + metadata, preserves seeds.
packages/emulate/src/api.ts:95-101: deletes tokenMap entries where user.installation is set, then store.reset() clears the github.installation_token_metadata collection (core/src/store.ts:251-256), then re-seeds. Seeded tokens (no installation field, api.ts:44-52, core/src/server.ts:33-41) and the materialized App private key survive; fallback-token behavior is per-request middleware (core/src/middleware/auth.ts:110-113) and unaffected. All asserted in packages/emulate/src/__tests__/api.test.ts:113-157.

3. Durable snapshots restore metadata + authorization consistently.
Metadata persists as collection github.installation_token_metadata (github/src/store.ts:119-122); adapters snapshot store + tokenMap in one atomic JSON blob (core/src/adapter-runtime.ts:97-109) and restore both (adapter-runtime.ts:110-131). Contract tests confirm restored inspection output is byte-equal and the restored token still authorizes (tests/contracts/github-app-identity.js:216-246).

4. Legacy snapshots compatible, no fabricated metadata.
Store.restore drops collections absent from a legacy snapshot (store.ts:271-276); the inspection route reads empty; authorization still works from restored tokenMap; a later mint lazily re-creates the collection via store.collection (store.ts:225-241) since apps.ts:197 calls getGitHubStore(store) fresh per request (no stale captured Collection reference). Covered by github-app-identity.js:247-282.

5. Mint atomicity/commit consistency.
Metadata insert (apps.ts:197-210) happens after all validation (permissions apps.ts:174-182, repo access apps.ts:184-191) and before tokenMap.set + 201 response. If insert throws, the handler 500s and no token is committed — proven by the mock-insert test (webhook-installation.test.ts:611-645: 500, zero ghs_ keys in tokenMap, empty inspection). Metadata and tokenMap get independent deep copies ({ ...requestedPermissions }, [...requestedRepoIds], apps.ts:205-206, 222-223), so no aliasing. One row per successful mint, rejected mints and seeded tokens not recorded (webhook-installation.test.ts:547-556, 559-596). Insert-before-token ordering means adapters persisting on mutating methods (adapter-runtime.ts:336-338) never save a token without its metadata.

6. Docs match behavior.
/docs/github/page.mdx:34-38 and skills/github/SKILL.md:613-620 accurately describe the payload, "secret-free", "expiry is informational and does not change authorization behavior", and the reset semantics; adapter paths (/emulate/github/_emulate/installation-tokens) match the plugin mount (github/src/index.ts:649, adapter-runtime.ts:335).

## Hardening observations (not defects)

- Unauthenticated, CORS-wildcard metadata endpoint. installation-tokens.ts has no auth gate, and the server mounts global cors() with default origin: "" (core/src/server.ts:48, core/src/http.ts:345-350). Any webpage in a browser can read org/account names, repo IDs, and granted permissions from a running emulator. No secrets leak, and the rest of the emulator surface is equally open (with a fallback user), but this is the first read-only introspection endpoint; if desired, gate it behind a header or restrict CORS for _emulate/.
- Orphaned metadata window. Metadata commits before the response is written; a crash between insert and response leaves a metadata row whose token no client holds. Observability-only; a GC matching rows against tokenMap on restore would tighten it.
- Unbounded growth. One metadata row per mint, never pruned; long-lived durable snapshots accumulate rows for expired tokens forever.

## Residual risks

1. Expired tokens remain fully authorized indefinitely in the emulator (pre-existing behavior, now explicitly documented as intentional — the metadata status: "expired" can mislead someone into thinking access lapsed).
2. Durable snapshots already contain minted token values and generated private keys (pre-existing from #205); the new metadata adds no sensitivity but increases what a leaked snapshot reveals about grants.
